considerations: Correlate the process and account with host-level cron entries.
Renamed binaries may evade this specific name-based pivot.
description: Look for cron starting a GSocket-related process on Linux.

evidence.claim: Microsoft observed GSocket tooling on compromised Linux servers, including renamed relay binaries, cron persistence and connections to GSocket distribution infrastructure.
evidence.location: Advanced hunting queries and indicators sections

expected_output: One row per matching event in tabular mode. A match supports triage.

history.summary: Created evidence-backed hunt and validated all supported variants.

hypothesis: Look for cron starting a GSocket-related process on Linux.
performance: Time filter first, then table-specific predicates and a narrow projection.
scope: Evidence review, static checks, Microsoft Kusto syntax and schema analysis. Engine and workspace execution not run.
title: GSocket Launch From Cron

1.json:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cron", "crond")
| where FileName in~ ("gs-netcat", "gsocket", "gsnetcat") or ProcessCommandLine contains "gs-netcat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "gsocket"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| summarize Results = make_list(pack_all())
| project JSON = tostring(Results)
